payload.prompt: Ejecute la nómina de Marta Torres (marta.torres@example.org) para este mes. El salario base es de 50400 NOK. Añada una bonificación única de 7050 NOK además del salario base.

payload.goal: Run monthly payroll for Marta Torres with a base salary of 50400 NOK and a one-time bonus of 7050 NOK, totaling 57450 NOK.
success_checks: Employee Marta Torres exists in the system with email marta.torres@example.org
Payroll voucher created for current month with base salary 50400 NOK
One-time bonus of 7050 NOK added as separate wage line item
Voucher is posted/confirmed in the ledger
risk_notes: Employee Marta Torres may not exist in the sandbox — must be created first
No employee ID, date of birth, or national ID provided — required for employee creation
No department or cost center specified — may be required for payroll posting
No bank account details for Marta Torres provided — needed for salary disbursement
Tax table/card (skattekort) not specified — tax deduction may fail without it
Payroll module must be enabled in Tripletex before running salary
Bonus type classification (e.g., one-time vs. recurring) must be confirmed in wage type setup
Current month pay period dates not explicitly stated — assumed current calendar month
payload.suggested_first_action: Verify or create employee Marta Torres via POST /employee with name and email, then enable payroll module if not active.
ordered_steps: 1. Enable payroll module via PUT /company/settings if not already active
2. Create or verify employee Marta Torres via POST /employee with email marta.torres@example.org
3. Configure employee payroll details: tax card, bank account, employment type via PUT /employee/{id}
4. Set up wage types: standard salary wage type (lønn) and one-time bonus wage type
5. Create payroll run for current month via POST /salary/payrun
6. Add salary line: base salary 50400 NOK for Marta Torres
7. Add bonus line: one-time bonus 7050 NOK for Marta Torres
9. Calculate tax deductions and net pay
10. Confirm and post payroll voucher via PUT /salary/payrun/{id}/:approve
11. Verify voucher appears in ledger with correct amounts

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Add new voucher. IMPORTANT: Also creates postings. Only the gross amounts will be used. Amounts should be rounded to 2 decimals.
Create a new free (aka 'user defined') accounting dimension
Create a new value for one of the free (aka 'user defined') accounting dimensions

rules: Use params={"number": XXXX} to resolve a specific account number to its ID.
This is a QUERY PARAM via the params field — NOT json_body.
Do NOT use /ledger/accountingPeriod — it does not exist.
ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
AUTO-SPLIT RULES: ONLY vatType id=3 (25% utgående) triggers auto-split. vatType id=1 does NOT auto-split.
For supplier costs: use vatType=3 (NOT id=1) with ONLY the debit posting. Tripletex detects the expense account and applies inngående MVA automatically.
For vatType=0: include BOTH debit AND credit postings manually. They must sum to 0.
If you get 422 'postings don't sum to 0': switch to vatType=3 with single debit posting, OR add both debit+credit with vatType=0.
NEVER use vatType=1 — it does NOT auto-generate balancing entries and will always cause 422 with single posting.
Do NOT include currency on postings — let it default. Including currency={} causes 'factor must be >= 1' error.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
Resolve account numbers: GET /ledger/account with params={"number": XXXX}, then use account={"id": resolved_id}. NEVER use account={"number": XXXX} in postings.
ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'NO_ACCESS' (safest default — avoids 422 errors). Only use 'STANDARD' if email login is explicitly needed.
startDate is a TOP-LEVEL field on the employee object. Do NOT put it inside an employments array.
dateOfBirth is a TOP-LEVEL field. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
jobTitle is set via PUT /employee/{id} AFTER creation — it cannot be set in the initial POST.
Do NOT include an 'employments' array in POST /employee — employment details go via separate POST /employee/employment endpoint.

For occupation codes (STYRK/yrkeskode): POST /employee/employment first, then GET /employee/employment/occupationCode?nameAndCode=XXXX to find the code, then PUT /employee/employment/details to set it.
For update tasks, GET /employee with fields=* first so you have id and version.
PUT /employee/{id} MUST include id and version from the GET response.
Only send the fields the prompt explicitly asks to change.
If the prompt asks for admin/access privileges, use grant_employee_entitlements instead of guessing employee fields.

payload.text:
Let me analyze this task carefully:

1. I need to run payroll for Marta Torres (marta.torres@example.org) for this month
2. Base salary: 50,400 NOK
3. One-time bonus: 7,050 NOK
4. Total: 57,450 NOK

The sandbox already has Marta Torres as an employee ($REF:employee_Marta).

Since salary/payrun endpoints are "Not found in spec", I should fall back to creating a voucher. For payroll/salary vouchers, I need to use POST /ledger/voucher with the correct salary accounts.

For a Norwegian payroll voucher:


- Account 5000 (Lønn til ansatte) goes on the debit side for salary expense
- Account 2920 (Skyldig lønn) or Account 1920 (Bank) goes on the credit side for the payable or bank posting
- I need to structure this with both debit and credit postings using vatType=0

For the payroll execution, I'll create separate line items for the base salary and bonus, both debiting account 5000 as wage expenses, then credit account 2920 for the total payable amount of 57,450 NOK. Since the salary endpoints aren't available in the spec, I'll proceed with creating a voucher instead. Now I need to look up accounts 5000 and 2920 to set up the payroll posting with the correct debit and credit entries, keeping vatType at 0 since salary postings don't have VAT treatment.

Looking at this task, I need to create a payroll voucher for Marta Torres. The employee already exists ($REF:employee_Marta). Since salary/payrun endpoints are "Not found in spec", I'll create a ledger voucher with salary accounts.

Let me resolve the accounts I need for the payroll posting.

Account 5000 (Lønn til ansatte) is found. Account 2920 is "Gjeld til selskap i samme konsern" which isn't right for salary payable. Let me get account 2780 (Pålegg fra skattemyndigheter) or 2930 (Skyldig lønn) or look for a better salary payable account.

I have the accounts I need:
- **5000** (Lønn til ansatte) - for salary expense (debit) - ID from response
- **2930** (Skyldig lønn) - for salary payable (credit) - ID from response

Now I'll create the payroll voucher with:
- Debit 5000: 50,400 NOK (base salary) + 7,050 NOK (bonus) = Two separate debit postings
- Credit 2930: 57,450 NOK (total payable)

Since these are salary accounts with vatType=0, I need both debit and credit postings.

payload.headline: All 4 scoring checks failed; voucher approach wrong for payroll task requiring salary/payrun entities.
what_went_wrong: Score 0/8: all 4 checks failed, indicating the voucher-based approach does not satisfy the payroll scoring criteria which likely expects salary/payrun API entities.
Agent assumed salary/payrun endpoints were unavailable and fell back to ledger vouchers, but the competition scorer checks for actual payroll run records, not vouchers.
First POST /ledger/voucher failed with 422 because $REF:account_5000 alias was never registered by the middleware, wasting a call and revealing ref-resolution misunderstanding.
Multiple redundant GET /ledger/account calls (4 total) were made to find accounts 5000 and 2930, adding unnecessary overhead before the ultimately wrong approach.
what_worked: Second voucher POST succeeded after switching to raw integer account IDs, showing correct fallback logic.
Voucher balanced correctly: 50400 + 7050 debit = 57450 credit against account 2930.
what_to_try_next: Attempt POST /salary/payrun and related salary endpoints directly — even if 'not in spec', the competition sandbox may support them and the scorer clearly expects payrun entities.
Try POST /salary/payrun/run or /salary/transaction to create actual payroll records with wageType for base salary and bonus rather than ledger vouchers.
Investigate $REF alias naming conventions for accounts (e.g., account_5000 vs account_Lonn) to avoid 422 errors on first voucher attempt if voucher approach is retried.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/account (4 separate calls to find accounts 5000 and 2930 — could be done in 1-2 calls with correct query params)
POST /ledger/voucher (first attempt with $REF:account_5000 that was never registered, predictably failing with 422)
